title: The Meadow Detectives and the Nibbled Bushes
markdown:
Oh, what a kerfuffle. Aria the seed collector — hair as sunny as a dandelion, pockets that jingle-jangled with tiny treasures — scrunched her nose. The berry bushes in Willow Creek Meadow looked wimpy. Plump branches a bit bare. Leaves with ragged holes. “Gran Ruth! They’re not as berry-full. A very busy, very nibbly visitor.”

Gran Ruth, a badger whose fur shimmered like moonbeams, shuffled over, paws soft on the grass. “They do seem a tad eaten. Miso agrees.”

Miso, a mouse with whiskers faster than a butterfly’s wings, nodded. “Squish! Less berries. Fewer crunchy seeds on the ground. My favourite bits.”

Aria felt a zippy idea. “Meadow detectives. Keep the bushes safe. Find who’s eating.”

First she tried protector: a sturdy twig fence, twined with grass, looking almost professional if you were a twig. Thump. A fluffy brown rabbit hopped right over, ears like antennas, munch-munch on bright green leaves, and paused to look insulted that anyone had bothered. The fence had not worked. It leaned, embarrassed.

Next, scare the birds. “Shoo!” A robin, chest puffed, about to peck a ripe red berry, tilted its head, chirped a surprised tune, and flew to a nearby branch, confused, then came back for the same berry as if the clap had been applause. Scaring was not working either. Aria’s pockets jingled with unused plans.

Dejected, Aria sat under a wide oak. Ruth sat beside her. Miso peeked from a pocket. “Everyone is eating the bushes.”

Ruth chuckled, warm thunder. “Look closely. What exactly is everyone eating?”

Mr. Rabbit still munched leaves. Miso pointed. “The squirrel!” Bushy tail, quick paws — not the plump berries. Dried bits that had fallen. Sniff, cheeks, scamper to hide them. “The seeds that dropped!”

The robin flew down and pecked a ripe berry.

Aria understood. “Not the whole bush. Different parts. Rabbit: leaves. Squirrel: fallen seeds. Robin: juicy berries. Favourite snacks from the same plant.”

Ruth smiled. Leaves for a growing rabbit. Fallen seeds stored for winter. Berries for flying energy. She left the dear-Aria off.

“They’re being shared. A picnic.” Aria pulled sunflower seeds from last week and shiny oat grains from a farmer’s cart. “If we leave other food, they might take less from the bushes.”

Miso pointed out spots. Ruth offered quiet nods. Aria scattered seeds near the rabbit’s nibble-place, near the clover where the squirrel hid treasures. The robin swooped for the new bits with a happy chirp.

She named the idea once — a food chain, plants at the start — without a never-ending-circle sermon or a hunt for more meadow secrets. Sharing extras kept bushes plumper and creatures fed.

Miso wiggled. “More food for all. Squish-squash-yum.”

Aria scooped a smooth brown seed from her pocket and did not announce she could not wait. She left a small pile under the oak, labelled in her head: not berries. The bushes, given a little less attention, looked almost ready to be berry-full again.
